body:
**If you get seasick easily, start by comparing a shorter Kleftiko trip with a small-group catamaran cruise. Choose according to the route, expected conditions and time aboard—not just the boat label.**

A catamaran can offer more space and comfortable seating, but it cannot guarantee a nausea-free day. A speedboat may shorten the journey without making it gentler.

If previous boat trips have made you severely ill, keeping a land-based day as your alternative is a reasonable choice.

## What travellers actually report

Apparently contradictory accounts can both be true.

In a [Reddit discussion about seasickness on Milos boat tours](https://www.reddit.com/r/GreeceTravel/comments/1k0bgv7/seasick_on_boat_tours_in_milos/), one passenger described a comfortable catamaran outing after the departure moved to the southeast side of the island. Another described an unpleasant initial passage on a catamaran and a route change that meant missing Kleftiko. A third reported being fine on a sailing boat.

These are individual experiences, not a survey. They show why someone else being comfortable on a particular boat cannot settle your choice.

Booking reviews also need context. A report of a comfortable outing is not a forecast for your departure. Read accounts of route changes as well as positive reviews, and ask the operator what would happen in the conditions expected for your trip.

The useful question is not simply “Did other people enjoy it?” It is “What route and conditions did they experience?”

## What you can confirm before booking

### The route may change with the wind

[Polco Sailing’s published information](https://www.polco-sailing.com/faq/) describes adjusting cruises to the more protected side of Milos. It also recommends leaving room in your stay for rescheduling.

That is useful flexibility, but shelter is something the skipper assesses for the conditions. It is not a guarantee attached to a particular beach or departure point.

A trip that goes ahead may still feel uncomfortable to you. Ask what the alternative itinerary would be, especially if Kleftiko is your main reason for booking.

### “Half-day” does not tell you how long the passages are

The listings checked for this guide include a four-hour shared Kleftiko outing, a five-hour private sailboat trip and a West Milos catamaran cruise lasting approximately eight to nine hours.

Those are total excursion durations, including stops.

Before paying, ask:

**“What is the longest continuous passage on the planned route, and approximately how much of the excursion is spent travelling?”**

A shorter outing may suit your tolerance better. It does not automatically mean calmer water.

### Cancellation terms depend on your booking

When rechecked on 16 October 2026, all three linked Viator product pages stated a full-refund cancellation deadline of 24 hours before the experience. This is a listing-level observation, not confirmation of the terms for an unselected date or option. Direct-booking conditions can differ.

Read the terms attached to your chosen departure. Also distinguish the operator cancelling the trip from you deciding not to travel.

If the itinerary changes but the excursion still runs, do not assume that you can cancel for a refund. Ask before booking.

For a broader comparison of the ride and itinerary, see [Milos Kleftiko: Sailboat or Speedboat?](/milos-kleftiko-sailboat-or-speedboat/).

## Catamaran, sailboat or speedboat?

### Catamaran: worth comparing for space and comfort

A catamaran is my first comparison if you want room to sit comfortably, shaded space and a less cramped day.

Polco describes its catamarans as more spacious than its monohulls. That is an operator’s description of its fleet, rather than evidence that passengers are less likely to become seasick.

The main trade-off is the itinerary. A comfortable layout does not compensate for a longer day than you want.

**Choose a catamaran if onboard space matters and you are comfortable with the advertised duration.** Check the route before committing to a full-day cruise.

### Sailboat: judge the particular trip

A monohull sailing boat is not automatically a poor choice. Milos travellers have reported comfortable sailboat outings.

A shorter private south-coast trip may also fit your needs better than a much longer shared excursion.

Ask about shaded seating with a horizon view, the planned passages and whether the trip involves sailing, motoring or both.

**Choose a sailboat when the actual itinerary and onboard arrangements suit you.** Do not assume that the word “sailing” means a gentler ride.

### Speedboat or RIB: faster needs a separate comfort check

If you dislike prolonged travel, a faster boat can sound appealing. But a shorter passage and a comfortable passage are different things.

I would consider this option only after the operator explains the expected ride, seating and route for the conditions.

If jolting movement is something you already find unpleasant, say so before booking.

**Consider a speedboat if you usually tolerate that kind of ride and want less time travelling.** The evidence reviewed does not justify calling it the best option for seasickness.

## Which option fits your situation?

### You mainly want Kleftiko and dislike long boat days

Start with a shorter, focused outing.

Confirm the longest passage, the departure point and how you will get there. A beach departure may involve an additional transfer cost.

### You want more space and shade

Compare a small-group catamaran.

Check the actual passenger limit and total duration. “Small group” is worth confirming rather than accepting as a label.

### You want more say over the day

Compare a private trip with a skipper.

Before paying extra, ask whether a shorter route or an earlier return can be agreed. A private booking does not automatically include either.

### You have experienced severe seasickness before

Keep a land-based alternative.

If the forecast and the operator’s explanation do not sound acceptable to you, you do not have to spend a day aboard to prove that you can manage it.

## A little preparation helps

The [CDC’s motion-sickness guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/travel-air-sea/motion-sickness.html) supports looking at the horizon, avoiding reading or screen use, and avoiding locations with the most movement, such as the bow.

Ask the crew where you can sit safely with a good outside view. Poor sleep and alcohol can make motion sickness worse.

If you may need medication, discuss it with a pharmacist or clinician before the trip. Prevention medicines generally work best before exposure, and they can have side effects or contraindications.

Someone else’s successful remedy is not a prescription for you.

## Dan’s choice

For a seasickness-prone visitor whose main goal is Kleftiko, **I would first compare a shorter south-coast outing and discuss the expected conditions with the operator.**

If space and shade matter more than keeping the day short, I would then compare a small-group catamaran.

I would pay extra for a private trip only if the operator confirms flexibility that would help me.

The best booking is the one whose route, duration and conditions you understand before paying.

## Three options worth comparing

*If you book through an affiliate link on this page, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.*

### Shorter shared outing: Zefiros Kleftiko tour

Viator product **420612P1**, supplied by Zefiros, describes approximately four hours from Agia Kyriaki. Its meeting information offers a transfer for an extra charge; arrange it in advance if needed.

This is the first comparison if you want a smaller time commitment. However, its published maximum is 100 travellers, so it should not be treated as a small-group cruise.

Confirm shaded seating, likely attendance and transport to the departure beach.

[Zefiros Kleftiko tour](https://www.viator.com/tours/Milos/Zefiros-half-day-tour-to-Kleftiko-Milos/d22323-420612P1?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

### More space, longer day: Polco West Milos catamaran

Viator product **32830P6**, supplied by Polco Sailing, describes an approximately eight-to-nine-hour catamaran cruise from Adamas, with shade and a maximum of 12 travellers.

It suits readers who are comfortable committing most of a day. **The passenger cap needs confirmation:** Viator says 12, while [Polco’s FAQ](https://www.polco-sailing.com/faq/) describes the West Milos cruise as accommodating up to 10. Ask which boat and limit apply to your departure.

Also ask which itinerary would operate if the wind makes the planned route unsuitable.

[Polco West Milos catamaran](https://www.viator.com/tours/Milos/West-Milos-Cruise-with-NIKI-L/d22323-32830P6?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

### Private shorter trip: sailboat from Agia Kyriaki

Viator product **272308P1**, supplied by **Milos VIP Services**, is the **Half-Day Private Romantic Sailing Getaway to Kleftiko**: approximately five hours from Agia Kyriaki, with tender boarding from the beach. It is listed as a private activity, not a self-drive rental.

It is worth comparing if discussing the day directly matters to you. A shorter route or early return still needs agreement before payment. The listing requires moderate physical fitness and is not wheelchair-accessible; confirm whether tender boarding suits you. Cave visits also need confirmation for the day.

[Milos VIP Services private Kleftiko sailboat](https://www.viator.com/tours/Milos/Romantic-Sailing-Getaway-to-Kleftiko-Best-experience-for-the-best-price/d22323-272308P1?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

**Start with the shorter outing if duration is your main worry. Compare the catamaran if space matters more. Choose private when the agreed flexibility is worth the extra cost to you.**

*Originally researched on 14 October 2026; product identities, linked listings and sources rechecked on 16 October 2026. No date-specific availability or final price has been confirmed. Routes, passenger limits and booking terms can change. This guide is based on published information and traveller accounts, rather than a personal test of these trips.*
